limits: Grok output is reviewed development input, not product runtime or whole-product approval
Native test profiles are fictional; no user/customer memory read

Same-OS-user/admin tampering of helper-owned private paths is outside the filesystem isolation guarantee.
Native stage_write can replace a pending pathname and ignores the helper review lock; MemoryStore mutations cooperate only on the target .lock.
Config/pending/current are rechecked immediately before memory write, not as an OS multi-file transaction.
Helper is host-only with HMAC key via stdin; HTTP cannot select paths, key, profile, or runtime.
Omitted helpers (_write_receipt, _parse_pending, _finish_remove_pending, _apply_dry, _file_lock, contextmanager wrappers) are review context, not independently verified here.

_cmd_decide handles phase=final only before the target lock; a concurrent waiter that missed that check can see unavailable/stale-review. HMAC beforeDigest blocks a second memory write; a later call that sees final remains idempotent.
recoveryReview.scope: Bounded recovery/decision functions in prompt; omitted helpers not independently re-reviewed. Later control-character and byte-limit checks do not change the audited recovery algorithm.
